A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPO study. The main sections, algorithm, equations, figure, tables, and complete Appendices A–B are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original experiments on materials deformation, topological materials deformation, and octa-alanine molecular dynamics, with results in Table 1 and Figure 1.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original experiments on all three problems, including numerical evaluation costs and trajectory plots.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same stage-wise sampling, replay memory, smooth L1 training of the scoring network, and automatic differentiation to obtain the policy. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same boundary deformation, level-set topological deformation, and octa-alanine dynamics tasks, with unchanged representations and starting distributions.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain TRPO, PPO, SAC, and their Straight negative-energy-reward variants on all three problems. Discussed model-based methods remain unevaluated.

E3.justification: Section 5.4 and Table 2 retain 200 test episodes, training budgets of 5000/5000/800 episodes, 20/20/6 steps, the same magnification factors, and unchanged evaluation costs.

E4.justification: The same cost-versus-time trajectory comparisons are retained. No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity analyses, or additional case studies are added or removed; both appendices remain theoretical.

E5.justification: Figure 1 retains identical uncertainty displays and their accompanying description. Neither version provides additional seed counts, repeated-training information, interval definitions, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All 21 numerical entries in Table 1 and all three Figure 1 plot images are identical. DPO's final costs remain 6.323, 6.061, and 53.340, preserving its lowest-cost ranking on each task.

T1.justification: Lemma 3, both in Section 3 and Appendix B, adds that g is as in Lemma 2, explicitly incorporating its target-function regularity conditions. The claimed bounds and proof arguments otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: differential RL/DPO, pointwise convergence, conditional regret bounds, and effectiveness on three configuration-search problems. Stronger abstract wording introduces no new guarantee.

C2.justification: Both retain the interpretation linking pointwise learning to physically consistent trajectories and the same discussion of why certain model-based methods cannot use the assumed black-box interface. No substantive interpretation or limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: New Section 7.5 explains that the experimental data are generated through black-box environments and can be regenerated using the existing repository. The code address, A100 hardware disclosure, and experimental parameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Bajaj and Nguyen's stochastic Hamiltonian dynamics learning and Bajaj, Li and Nguyen's protein side-chain packing work, cited in the introduction and molecular-dynamics discussion. The other cited works and overall positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract and introduction, refines terminology such as 'learned deformation operator,' adds keywords and a Declarations section, and revises author information. The research-section sequence and most technical prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout: the title/abstract page is redesigned, page geometry and typography change, running headers are replaced by footer numbering, and tables, captions, and mathematical passages are reflowed. Figure 1 and Tables 1–2 retain their contents.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves precision by explicitly linking Lemma 3 to Lemma 2's conditions and improves reproducibility documentation by explaining data regeneration. The method, proof arguments, and experimental evidence remain unchanged, so the quality gain is limited despite extensive reformatting.
